prompt_en: An observational environmental portrait shows electricity visibly at work through visible electrical discharges. The woman follows the supplied reference for her facial appearance and hairstyle, retaining its slender oval face, large almond-shaped gray-brown eyes, natural brows, softly full lips, and short dark brown bob with fine wispy bangs. She is qualifying a restored portable teaching rig in an after-hours university demonstration room. The photograph catches the first test that has worked well enough for her to lift her attention from the logbook to the apparatus. On the left side of the bench, an electrostatic generator with two vertical glass disks feeds two polished spherical electrodes set several centimeters apart. On this restored travelling rig, a short irregular luminous channel bridges two nearby metal tips, the rounded terminal surfaces of the two conducting spheres. This blue-white spark spans their open air gap; both channel endpoints meet those tips, and the surrounding air stays darker than the channel. To its right, the separately powered neon apparatus stands on ceramic mounts: a translucent glass tube encloses a broad soft luminous gas region, whose orange-red emission continuously follows the narrow curved bore. The two dark electrode caps define the ends of the same curved carrier: two end electrodes belong to that tube, and dark glass margins remain outside the luminous region. Black insulated leads meet the tube's two electrode caps and run back to its compact supply. The spark and the glowing tube are separated in space and clearly differ in color, carrier, and shape. A transparent apparatus cover sits between these devices and the operator's console, its edges and reflections staying subordinate to the electrical phenomena. The woman stands on the console side in a soft ivory sleeveless knit top and charcoal utility trousers. Her left hand rests on the near edge of the console; her right hand holds a pencil just above an open logbook. Her gaze has just lifted toward the spark, and concentration is giving way to a small relieved half-smile. The tilt of her head exposes the familiar face rather than presenting a stock technician pose. In the lower foreground, an open travelling case cradles a removed blackened tube collar and a clean spare tube, while the newly fitted collar remains visible on the glowing apparatus. Pencil traces in the log, the discarded collar, and the ready case connect this living moment to the repair and to the demonstrator's next journey. Make a landscape 3:2 photograph with a natural 35 mm perspective, viewed from chest height at a gentle three-quarter angle. Arrange the apparatus to the left, her face to the right, and the hands and logbook lower between them. Keep the face, spark endpoints, and curved glass wall sufficiently resolved to read together. A warm task lamp gives her cheek and the knit a quiet tactile presence; the small blue-white spark and the orange-red tube emit their own localized light. Preserve natural skin texture, clear glass reflections, dark metal detail, and the difference between a brief air discharge and a sustained glow inside glass.
